```{r}
#| label: changelog-2-0-0-data
#| include: false

# The numbers of this section are pinned to the two releases it compares:
#   2.0.0 from its saved counts (R/Website/save_version_counts.R), 1.0.0
#   from the reference counts of the validation stage. Neither database is
#   opened, so a later release does not change this section. Numbers of
#   one-off checks are written out in the text with a link to their source
data_counts_2_0_0 <-
  readr::read_csv(
    file = here::here("Data/Versions/2.0.0/database_counts.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

data_counts_1_0_0 <-
  readr::read_csv(
    file = here::here("Data/Validation/v1.0.0_reference_counts.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(n = "n_v1")

data_query_times_2_0_0 <-
  readr::read_csv(
    file = here::here("Data/Versions/2.0.0/vaultkeepr_query_times.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

# Short local helpers: the text of this section prints many counts of the
#   two releases, and these keep each inline expression readable
count_1_0_0 <- function(metric, scope) {
  select_version_count(data_counts_1_0_0, metric, scope)
}

count_2_0_0 <- function(metric, scope) {
  select_version_count(data_counts_2_0_0, metric, scope)
}

# The v1.0.0 database file (VegVault.sqlite of the deposit
#   https://doi.org/10.48700/datst.t21cz-2nq07), in bytes, as read from
#   the file on the build computer before the 2.0.0 release build
size_bytes_1_0_0 <- 110036815872

size_bytes_2_0_0 <-
  count_2_0_0("size_bytes", "database")

ratio_size_2_0_0 <-
  size_bytes_1_0_0 / size_bytes_2_0_0

# Query times: the old combination (vaultkeepr 0.1.0 on 1.0.0) against the
#   new one (vaultkeepr 0.2.0 on 2.0.0), for the workflows of both
data_times_old <-
  data_query_times_2_0_0 |>
  dplyr::filter(
    database_version == "1.0.0",
    vaultkeepr_version == "0.1.0"
  )

data_times_new <-
  data_query_times_2_0_0 |>
  dplyr::filter(
    database_version == "2.0.0",
    vaultkeepr_version == "0.2.0"
  )

data_times_paired <-
  dplyr::inner_join(
    dplyr::select(data_times_old, "workflow", seconds_old = "seconds_median"),
    dplyr::select(data_times_new, "workflow", seconds_new = "seconds_median"),
    by = "workflow"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = seconds_old / seconds_new)

seconds_old_total <-
  base::sum(dplyr::pull(data_times_paired, seconds_old))

seconds_new_total <-
  base::sum(dplyr::pull(data_times_paired, seconds_new))

ratio_speed_2_0_0 <-
  seconds_old_total / seconds_new_total

seconds_traits_original_1_0_0 <-
  data_query_times_2_0_0 |>
  dplyr::filter(
    workflow == "traits_bolivia",
    database_version == "1.0.0",
    vaultkeepr_version == "0.2.0"
  ) |>
  dplyr::pull(seconds_median)

seconds_traits_original_2_0_0 <-
  data_times_new |>
  dplyr::filter(workflow == "traits_bolivia") |>
  dplyr::pull(seconds_median)

n_trait_datasets_2_0_0 <-
  count_2_0_0("datasets", "traits / BIEN") +
  count_2_0_0("datasets", "traits / TRY")

label_count <-
  scales::label_comma()

# Sizes in decimal gigabytes, without a trailing zero (6.5 GB, 110 GB)
label_size <-
  scales::label_number(
    accuracy = 0.1,
    scale = 1e-9,
    suffix = " GB",
    drop0trailing = TRUE
  )

label_seconds <-
  scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.01)

label_ratio <-
  scales::label_number(accuracy = 1)

label_percent <-
  scales::label_percent(accuracy = 0.1)
```

[VegVault]{.vegvault} 2.0.0 is the second release.
It is rebuilt from tagged, checksum-verified releases of the [vegetation]{.neo-vegetation}, [fossil pollen]{.paleo}, [trait]{.traits} and [abiotic data]{.abiotic}, with audited [trait units]{.traits} and a corrected linkage of [gridpoints]{.abiotic} to samples.
It is also about `r label_ratio(ratio_size_2_0_0)` times smaller than 1.0.0 (`r label_size(size_bytes_2_0_0)` instead of `r label_size(size_bytes_1_0_0)`) and, read with [{vaultkeepr}](https://bit.ly/vaultkeepr) 0.2.0, about `r label_ratio(ratio_speed_2_0_0)` times faster to query than 1.0.0 was with {vaultkeepr} 0.1.0.
Its [SQLite database]{.database} ([10.48700/y3p8y-g8106](https://doi.org/10.48700/y3p8y-g8106)) and its flat files ([10.48700/gpf0m-ptq85](https://doi.org/10.48700/gpf0m-ptq85)) are deposited in the [EOSC CZ data repository](https://datarepo.eosc.cz/) as new versions of the 1.0.0 records.

::: {.callout-tip title="Moving from 1.0.0 to 2.0.0"}
Running the same code with [VegVault]{.vegvault} 2.0.0 and {vaultkeepr} 0.2.0 may return different data than with [VegVault]{.vegvault} 1.0.0 and {vaultkeepr} 0.1.0.
The sections below describe what changed.
:::

### Changes at a glance {#v2-0-0-glance .topic-database}

| Change | For code written for 1.0.0 | Section |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Database]{.database} ids are numbered anew; BIEN plot [datasets]{.database}, [fossil pollen]{.paleo} samples and [trait]{.traits} samples have new names | **Breaks code** that keeps ids or names from 1.0.0 | [Identifiers and names](#v2-0-0-identifiers) |
| [Soil groups]{.abiotic} come from HWSD v2.2, with new codes | **Breaks code** that looks up [soil]{.abiotic} codes | [Climate and soil](#v2-0-0-abiotic) |
| The flat files have no file of `AbioticDataReference` | **Breaks code** that reads that file | [The schema](#v2-0-0-schema) |
| The unit label of `bio4` is corrected | **Breaks code** that matches the label text | [Climate and soil](#v2-0-0-abiotic) |
| BIEN [trait]{.traits} records that name no provider have no data source | **Breaks code** that requires a data source for every record | [Plant traits](#v2-0-0-traits) |
| `bio4`, [trait units]{.traits} and a [precipitation]{.abiotic} artefact are corrected | Changes results | [Climate and soil](#v2-0-0-abiotic), [Plant traits](#v2-0-0-traits) |
| Links follow the documented rule exactly | Changes results: more links at high latitudes and across the dateline | [Links between samples and gridpoints](#v2-0-0-links) |
| [Taxon names]{.taxa} are classified again | Changes results | [Vegetation, fossil pollen and taxa](#v2-0-0-taxa) |
| New content of the sources: [fossil pollen]{.paleo}, BIEN [vegetation plots]{.neo-vegetation}, [TRY]{.traits} values | Changes results | [Vegetation, fossil pollen and taxa](#v2-0-0-taxa), [Plant traits](#v2-0-0-traits) |
| `AbioticDataReference` is a view; new tables and columns; keys, checks and indexes | Nothing to do | [The schema](#v2-0-0-schema) |
| {vaultkeepr} 0.1.0 still reads 2.0.0 | Nothing breaks, but use {vaultkeepr} 0.2.0 | [Which {vaultkeepr} reads which version](#v2-0-0-vaultkeepr) |

### Smaller and faster {#v2-0-0-speed .topic-database}

The [database]{.database} file is `r label_size(size_bytes_2_0_0)` (`r label_count(size_bytes_2_0_0)` bytes) against `r label_size(size_bytes_1_0_0)` for 1.0.0, mostly because the links between samples and [gridpoints]{.abiotic} are stored once per position (see [The schema](#v2-0-0-schema)).

The nine example workflows of the {vaultkeepr} articles were timed from opening the [database]{.database} to the extracted table, each five times, taking turns with the others, on one computer (24 cores, 64 GB RAM) on 2026-11-26 ([benchmark on VegVault issue 84](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/issues/84#issuecomment-7191319116)).
The table gives the median time in seconds.
{vaultkeepr} 0.1.0 did not run the workflows marked "not run": its geographic window does not apply to [trait datasets]{.traits}, which these workflows would then include from the whole world, so their results cannot be compared (see [Which {vaultkeepr} reads which version](#v2-0-0-vaultkeepr)).

```{r}
#| label: changelog-2-0-0-query-times
#| echo: false

data_query_times_2_0_0 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    run = stringr::str_c(
      "{vaultkeepr} ", vaultkeepr_version, " on ", database_version
    ),
    seconds = label_seconds(seconds_median)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select("workflow", "description", "run", "seconds") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = "run",
    values_from = "seconds",
    values_fill = "not run"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    base::match(workflow, dplyr::pull(data_times_new, workflow))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    "description",
    "{vaultkeepr} 0.1.0 on 1.0.0",
    "{vaultkeepr} 0.2.0 on 1.0.0",
    "{vaultkeepr} 0.2.0 on 2.0.0"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Workflow",
      "{vaultkeepr} 0.1.0 on 1.0.0",
      "{vaultkeepr} 0.2.0 on 1.0.0",
      "{vaultkeepr} 0.2.0 on 2.0.0"
    ),
    align = "lrrr"
  )
```

The workflows that both versions of {vaultkeepr} ran took `r label_seconds(seconds_old_total)` s together with {vaultkeepr} 0.1.0 on 1.0.0 and `r label_seconds(seconds_new_total)` s with {vaultkeepr} 0.2.0 on 2.0.0, about `r label_ratio(ratio_speed_2_0_0)` times faster; single workflows ran between `r label_ratio(base::min(dplyr::pull(data_times_paired, ratio)))` and `r label_ratio(base::max(dplyr::pull(data_times_paired, ratio)))` times faster.
Most of the gain comes from {vaultkeepr} 0.2.0, which narrows a query to the selected samples before it classifies [taxa]{.taxa} or reads references and age uncertainty: with the same {vaultkeepr} 0.2.0, most workflows take about as long on 2.0.0 as on 1.0.0.
One query is slower on 2.0.0: `get_traits()` with its default, the original [taxon names]{.taxa}, took `r label_seconds(seconds_traits_original_2_0_0)` s against `r label_seconds(seconds_traits_original_1_0_0)` s on 1.0.0, because {vaultkeepr} 0.2.0 joins all [trait values]{.traits} with the new unit tables before it narrows them to the selection ([vaultkeepr issue 77](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/vaultkeepr/issues/77)).

### Which {vaultkeepr} reads which version {#v2-0-0-vaultkeepr .topic-reproducibility}

{vaultkeepr} 0.2.0 reads both [VegVault]{.vegvault} 1.0.0 and 2.0.0.
It opens the [database]{.database} read-only and reads its version when it opens it.
With 2.0.0, `get_traits()` also returns the unit of each [trait value]{.traits} and the keys of the rules that converted or derived it (`trait_unit`, `conversion_rule_key` and `derivation_rule_key`).

{vaultkeepr} 0.1.0 also opens a 2.0.0 [database]{.database}, runs without error and returns the same values for the same selection.
But its geographic window does not apply to [trait datasets]{.traits}: a [trait]{.traits} workflow returns all `r label_count(n_trait_datasets_2_0_0)` [trait datasets]{.traits} of the [database]{.database}, wherever they lie, and it is up to about 180 times slower than {vaultkeepr} 0.2.0 ([check on VegVault issue 84](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/issues/84#issuecomment-7164297853)).
Use {vaultkeepr} 0.2.0 with [VegVault]{.vegvault} 2.0.0.

### Identifiers and names {#v2-0-0-identifiers .topic-database}

- **[Database]{.database} ids are numbered anew in every build**, the [trait domains]{.traits} included.
  Ids saved from 1.0.0 cannot be joined to 2.0.0.
- **Some names changed:** BIEN plot [datasets]{.database} are named by their BIEN plot identifier (such as `bien_CTFS__P01`) instead of a row number (such as `bien_1`), [fossil pollen]{.paleo} samples by the Neotoma dataset id instead of the 1.0.0 [database]{.database} id (`fossilpol_91256_21011` became `fossilpol_1001_21011`), and [trait]{.traits} samples by the observation id of their source.
- **Unchanged:** the names of the [gridpoints]{.abiotic} (`geo_<long>_<lat>` and `geo_<long>_<lat>_<age>`), the names of the [trait domains]{.traits} (including "Plant heigh") and the names of the [abiotic variables]{.abiotic}.

Select your data again by place, age, dataset type or [taxon]{.taxa} rather than by saved ids or names.

### The schema {#v2-0-0-schema .topic-database}

The [database]{.database} has `r count_2_0_0("n_tables", "database")` tables, `r count_2_0_0("n_views", "database")` view and `r count_2_0_0("n_columns", "database")` columns.
The [Database Structure](database_structure.qmd) page describes each table.

- **Links are stored once per position.**
  A position is a place and age shared by samples.
  The new tables `Positions`, `SamplePosition` and `PositionLink` hold the links between positions and [gridpoints]{.abiotic}, and `AbioticDataReference`, a table in 1.0.0, is now a view with the same columns (`sample_id`, `sample_ref_id`, `distance_in_km` and `distance_in_years`), one row per sample and [gridpoint]{.abiotic}.
  Code that reads `AbioticDataReference` works as before.
- **The flat files have no file of `AbioticDataReference`**, because the view returns `r label_count(count_2_0_0("sample_links", "all"))` rows.
  Join `SamplePosition` and `PositionLink` by `position_id` instead: the result has the columns of the view.
- **New tables and columns for [trait units]{.traits}:** `TraitsDomain` has a `trait_unit`, and `TraitsValue` has `trait_unit_conversion_id` and `trait_derivation_id`, which point to the new tables `TraitUnitConversion` and `TraitDerivation` (see [Plant traits](#v2-0-0-traits)).
- **The build is recorded in the [database]{.database}:** `version_control` has the new columns `build_profile`, `git_commit` and `manifest_sha256` (the SHA-256 of the list of input files), and the new table `BuildProducers` lists every input of the build with its release tag.
- **Keys and checks:** [dataset]{.database} and sample names are unique and never empty, the link and reference tables have composite primary keys, [trait values]{.traits} are keyed on [dataset]{.database}, sample, [trait]{.traits} and [taxon]{.taxa}, and coordinates must lie on the globe.
  Of the 59 secondary indexes of 1.0.0, the 29 that repeat another index or key are dropped ([database design, decision 3](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/blob/v2.0.0/Documentation/Database_design_2.0.0.md#decisions-for-gate-g2)).
- **Unchanged on purpose:** the misspelt column `trait_domanin_description` of `TraitsDomain`, and the storage of [gridpoints]{.abiotic} as [datasets]{.database} and samples.

### Links between samples and gridpoints {#v2-0-0-links .topic-abiotic}

A sample is linked to a [gridpoint]{.abiotic} when the two are at most 50 km **and** at most 5,000 years apart.
1.0.0 used the same rule, but searched only within one degree of longitude and did not wrap at the dateline, so it missed some links.
2.0.0 applies the rule exactly.
Run on the 1.0.0 inputs, it keeps every link of 1.0.0, with the same distances, and adds 427,097 links (0.45%) at 6,572 positions: 420,983 at high latitudes, where 50 km is more than one degree of longitude, and 6,114 across the dateline ([comparison on VegVault issue 84](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/issues/84#issuecomment-7067924436)).

The view `AbioticDataReference` returns `r label_count(count_2_0_0("sample_links", "all"))` links in 2.0.0, against `r label_count(count_1_0_0("table_rows", "AbioticDataReference"))` rows of the table in 1.0.0.
Because the rule of 2.0.0 keeps every link of 1.0.0 on the same inputs, the lower total comes from the samples of 2.0.0, which differ from those of 1.0.0 (see the sections below).

### Climate and soil {#v2-0-0-abiotic .topic-abiotic}

- **`bio4` (temperature seasonality) is corrected.**
  In 1.0.0 it was 0 at age 0 at every [gridpoint]{.abiotic} south of about 65.7° N, because of a truncated download ([VegVault issue 78](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/issues/78)).
  This affects every [vegetation plot]{.neo-vegetation} and every [fossil pollen]{.paleo} sample that takes its [climate]{.abiotic} from age 0.
- **The unit label of `bio4`** is now "C/100 (hundredths of a degree Celsius)", which matches its values; in 1.0.0 it read "C (degree Celsius)".
  The values themselves were already in hundredths of a degree.
- **Present-day annual [precipitation]{.abiotic} (`bio12`) of 6,553.5 kg m⁻² is a lower bound.**
  CHELSA V2.1 stores it as whole numbers of 0.1 kg m⁻² of at most 65,535, so wetter places are stored as 6,553.5 kg m⁻² ([note on VegVault issue 84](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/issues/84#issuecomment-7067866097)).
  This is unchanged from 1.0.0, and now documented.
- **A [precipitation]{.abiotic} artefact of CHELSA-TraCE21k is masked:** `bio12`, `bio15`, `bio18` and `bio19` have no value in a block of South America (25° S to 5° N, 80° W to 35° W) at 12,000, 12,500 and 15,000 to 18,000 years before present, where the source shows inflated [precipitation]{.abiotic} ([note on VegVault issue 84](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/issues/84#issuecomment-7102156981)).
- **Zero [precipitation]{.abiotic} in dry seasons:** CHELSA-TraCE21k stores [precipitation]{.abiotic} in whole kg m⁻², so a quarter with less than 0.5 kg m⁻² is 0 in the past, while the present-day values come in steps of 0.1 kg m⁻² ([check on VegVault issue 96](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/issues/96#issuecomment-7127426672)).
  In the Sahel and the Sudanian belt, the coldest quarter of `bio19` can be the dry winter in one product and the rainy season in the other.
- **[Soil groups]{.abiotic} are rebuilt from HWSD v2.2**; 1.0.0 labelled them WoSIS and SoilGrids.
  The codes 1 to 32 of `HWSD2` are the WRB 2022 Reference Soil Groups in alphabetical order, and they cannot be compared with the codes of 1.0.0, which came from a wrong lookup ([note on VegVault issue 84](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/issues/84#issuecomment-7102156981)).
  The legend is `Outputs/Tables/hwsd_soil_group_legend.csv` in the [abiotic data repository](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-abiotic_data/releases/tag/v2.0.0).
  A [gridpoint]{.abiotic} whose dominant class is not a [soil]{.abiotic} (glaciers, open water) has no [soil]{.abiotic} value.
  2.0.0 has `r label_count(count_2_0_0("abiotic_values", "HWSD2"))` [soil]{.abiotic} values at [gridpoints]{.abiotic}, against `r label_count(count_1_0_0("abiotic_values", "HWSD2"))` in 1.0.0.

### Plant traits {#v2-0-0-traits .topic-traits}

- **Every [trait value]{.traits} is in one unit per [trait domain]{.traits}**, converted from the unit of its source by a recorded rule.
  `TraitUnitConversion` holds `r count_2_0_0("table_rows", "TraitUnitConversion")` conversion rules and `TraitDerivation` `r count_2_0_0("table_rows", "TraitDerivation")` derivation rule (leaf mass per area from specific leaf area).
  Some values differ from 1.0.0 by a unit factor; for example, leaf area is now in mm² instead of cm².
- **The audit of the units** is attached to the [trait data release](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-Trait_data/releases/tag/v2.0.0): a summary and a reconciliation of the units of each source (`trait_unit_audit_summary_*.csv` and `trait_unit_reconciliation_*.csv`), with the tables of the other checks of the [trait]{.traits} data ([VegVault issue 76](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/issues/76)).
- **[TRY]{.traits} is kept, with TRY's standardised values.**
  In 1.0.0, 45.6% of the [TRY]{.traits} values did not match the standardised value of their record.
  Repeated measurements are removed, including BIEN records that copy [TRY]{.traits} ([trait data release notes](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-Trait_data/releases/tag/v2.0.0)).
  The [TRY]{.traits} reference of each record is stored as a sample reference.
- **Counts:** `r label_count(count_2_0_0("traits_value_rows", "traits / TRY"))` [TRY]{.traits} values in `r label_count(count_2_0_0("datasets", "traits / TRY"))` [datasets]{.database} (1.0.0: `r label_count(count_1_0_0("traits_value_rows", "traits / TRY"))` in `r label_count(count_1_0_0("datasets", "traits / TRY"))`), and `r label_count(count_2_0_0("traits_value_rows", "traits / BIEN"))` BIEN values in `r label_count(count_2_0_0("datasets", "traits / BIEN"))` [datasets]{.database} (1.0.0: `r label_count(count_1_0_0("traits_value_rows", "traits / BIEN"))` in `r label_count(count_1_0_0("datasets", "traits / BIEN"))`).
  BIEN [trait]{.traits} samples without a value are dropped ([database design, decision 4](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/blob/v2.0.0/Documentation/Database_design_2.0.0.md#decisions-for-gate-g2)).
- **BIEN [trait]{.traits} records that name no provider have no data source.**
  The data source of a BIEN [trait]{.traits} record is the principal investigator of its BIEN project, and 7,869 BIEN plant-height values in 3,609 [datasets]{.database} name none.
  In 2.0.0 their `data_source_id` is empty; in 1.0.0 they pointed to a data source without a description, so neither version names their provider ([check on VegVault issue 167](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/issues/167#issuecomment-7196060171)).
  {vaultkeepr} returns `NA` as their `data_source_desc` in both versions, but code that joins every [dataset]{.database} to a data source drops these records in 2.0.0.

### Vegetation, fossil pollen and taxa {#v2-0-0-taxa .topic-taxa}

- **[Fossil pollen]{.paleo}:** a fresh download of the Neotoma Paleoecology Database and a full rerun of the FOSSILPOL workflow give `r label_count(count_2_0_0("datasets", "fossil_pollen_archive / FOSSILPOL"))` [datasets]{.database} with `r label_count(count_2_0_0("samples", "fossil_pollen_archive / FOSSILPOL"))` samples, against `r label_count(count_1_0_0("datasets", "fossil_pollen_archive / FOSSILPOL"))` and `r label_count(count_1_0_0("samples", "fossil_pollen_archive / FOSSILPOL"))` in 1.0.0 ([FOSSILPOL release notes](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-FOSSILPOL/releases/tag/v2.0.0)).
- **[Vegetation plots]{.neo-vegetation}:** every plot has at most one record per [taxon]{.taxa}, and re-surveyed BIEN plots keep only their latest survey: `r label_count(count_2_0_0("datasets", "vegetation_plot / BIEN"))` BIEN plots with `r label_count(count_2_0_0("sample_taxa_rows", "vegetation_plot / BIEN"))` [taxon]{.taxa} records, against `r label_count(count_1_0_0("datasets", "vegetation_plot / BIEN"))` and `r label_count(count_1_0_0("sample_taxa_rows", "vegetation_plot / BIEN"))` in 1.0.0, and the same `r label_count(count_2_0_0("datasets", "vegetation_plot / sPlotOpen"))` sPlotOpen plots in both versions ([vegetation data release notes](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-Vegetation_data/releases/tag/v2.0.0)).
- **[Taxon names]{.taxa} are classified again.**
  Two kinds of names are corrected by hand: the 116 [fossil pollen]{.paleo} types that combine two or more [taxa]{.taxa} (such as "Betula/Carpinus") keep only what their parts share, the family when all parts belong to one family (80 types) and no classification otherwise (36 types), and "Pinus Picea" is classified as Pinaceae instead of *Abies alba* ([decision record on VegVault issue 86](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/issues/86)).
  Some errors of 1.0.0 are gone: for example, 1.0.0 classified the pollen type *Alnus viridis* as the genus *Atanus*, a leafhopper ([comparison on vaultkeepr issue 51](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/vaultkeepr/issues/51#issuecomment-7156522751)).
- **Unclassified names:** `r label_count(count_2_0_0("n_taxa_unclassified", "database"))` of the `r label_count(count_2_0_0("table_rows", "Taxa"))` [taxon names]{.taxa} (`r label_percent(count_2_0_0("n_taxa_unclassified", "database") / count_2_0_0("table_rows", "Taxa"))`) have no classification.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="All counts of 1.0.0 and 2.0.0"}
The counts that the validation stage compares, from the reference counts of 1.0.0 and the saved counts of 2.0.0.
For 1.0.0, the links per sample are the rows of the table `AbioticDataReference`; for 2.0.0, the rows of the view.

```{r}
#| label: changelog-2-0-0-all-counts
#| echo: false

vec_metric_labels <-
  c(
    table_rows = "Rows of the table",
    datasets = "Datasets",
    samples = "Samples",
    positions = "Positions",
    sample_taxa_rows = "Taxon records",
    traits_value_rows = "Trait values",
    abiotic_values = "Abiotic values",
    sample_links = "Links between samples and gridpoints"
  )

dplyr::full_join(
  data_counts_1_0_0 |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      flag_links = metric == "table_rows" & scope == "AbioticDataReference",
      metric = dplyr::if_else(flag_links, "sample_links", metric),
      scope = dplyr::if_else(flag_links, "all", scope)
    ) |>
    dplyr::select("metric", "scope", n_1_0_0 = "n"),
  data_counts_2_0_0 |>
    dplyr::filter(scope != "database") |>
    dplyr::select("metric", "scope", n_2_0_0 = "n"),
  by = c("metric", "scope")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    base::match(metric, base::names(vec_metric_labels)),
    scope
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric = base::unname(vec_metric_labels[metric]),
    change = dplyr::if_else(
      base::is.na(n_1_0_0) | base::is.na(n_2_0_0),
      "-",
      label_percent((n_2_0_0 - n_1_0_0) / n_1_0_0)
    ),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = c("n_1_0_0", "n_2_0_0"),
      .fns = ~ dplyr::if_else(base::is.na(.x), "-", label_count(.x))
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Count", "Of", "1.0.0", "2.0.0", "Change"),
    align = "llrrr"
  )
```
:::
